html:
The Popoluca are several Indigenous peoples of southern Veracruz, Mexico, in the Sierra de Santa Marta and the lowlands around Sayula, Oluta and Texistepec. They speak languages of the Mixe-Zoque family, related to Mixe and Zoque. The name Popoluca is a Nahuatl word for people who speak a foreign tongue.

Their land lies in the old Olmec heartland, and many scholars think the Olmecs spoke an early Mixe-Zoque language. By the 1400s the Popoluca lived among Nahua towns that paid tribute to the Aztecs. They farm maize, beans and coffee on the slopes of the sierra. Tens of thousands of people still speak Popoluca languages.
